prs.title: promql: preserve quantile bucket for histograms with NaN sum
prs.body:
When a native histogram's sum is NaN, `HistogramQuantile` scans the remaining buckets to determine whether to report NaN observations. That scan overwrote the selected bucket, causing interpolation to use the last bucket instead. Preserve the selected bucket while accumulating the remaining counts.

For observations `{1.5, 3, NaN}`, `histogram_quantile(0.2, …)` returned approximately `3.0314` instead of `1.5157`.

Regression tests cover multiple populated buckets, native histograms with custom buckets, classic histogram controls, and corresponding `histogram_fraction` evaluations. The `-Inf`/`+Inf` case is covered using schema `-4`.

Five regression evaluations fail without the fix; the remaining controls pass either way.

Validation: focused PromQL tests, lint, race-enabled Go tests, generated parser check, and UI tests/lint passed.

#### Which issue(s) does the PR fix:

None.

prs.title: otlp: sort exemplars by timestamp before appending
prs.body:
The OTLP endpoint passed each data point's exemplars to the appender in the order they arrived. `AppenderV2` requires them sorted by timestamp, and the TSDB drops an exemplar that's older than one already appended for the same series, unless it's within the out-of-order time window. So when a data point carried an exemplar after a newer one, the older exemplar was dropped on commit.

This PR sorts each series' exemplars by timestamp before appending. Classic histogram buckets get their exemplars as before, and each bucket's exemplars are sorted.

#### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered).

```release-notes
[BUGFIX] OTLP: Stop dropping exemplars that arrive out of timestamp order within a data point.
```

prs.title: mixin: fix PrometheusRemoteStorageFailures denominator double-counting
prs.body:
### Which issue(s) does the PR fix:
Related to #19870

### What does this PR do?
Fixes a double-counting bug in the `PrometheusRemoteStorageFailures` alert denominator in `alerts.libsonnet`.

Previously, the fallback denominator expression evaluated to `(samples_failed_total + samples_total)`. Because `samples_total` already accounts for all sample send attempts (including those that fail), adding `samples_failed_total` resulted in double-counting failures (e.g., an all-failed batch with 0 retries yielded a 50% failure rate instead of 100%).

This PR updates the denominator logic to:

```promql
(
  (rate(prometheus_remote_storage_failed_samples_total{%(prometheusSelector)s}[5m]) + rate(prometheus_remote_storage_succeeded_samples_total{%(prometheusSelector)s}[5m]))
  or
  rate(prometheus_remote_storage_samples_total{%(prometheusSelector)s}[5m])
)
```

prs.title: agent: support metadata-wal-records in agent mode
prs.body:
#### Which issue(s) does the PR fix:

None

#### Overview / Description:

This PR adds support for the `--enable-feature=metadata-wal-records` feature flag in Prometheus Agent mode.

When enabled:
- **Ingestion**: Both `Appender.UpdateMetadata` and `AppenderV2.Append` (with metadata options) record `record.Metadata` entries to the Agent WAL and update in-memory series metadata on commit. Redundant metadata updates are deduplicated, and rollbacks discard pending metadata changes.
- **In-Memory Tracking**: `memSeries` and `seriesSnapshot` store series metadata and expose `Metadata() *metadata.Metadata`.
- **Checkpointing**: In-memory checkpointing (`agent.Checkpoint`) preserves series metadata as `record.Metadata` records in checkpoints, matching `wlog.Checkpoint`.
- **WAL Replay**: During WAL replay, `record.Metadata` records are decoded and mapped to their respective series.

prs.title: scrape: do not use invalid native histograms for start timestamp synthesis
prs.body:
In the experimental start timestamp synthesis (`st-synthesis`), a scraped histogram became the anchor before the append path validated it. If a target exposed a histogram with an invalid bucket layout, later samples were compared with and subtracted from it. For example, when a later sample had a lower schema, the subtraction panicked in `mustReduceResolution`. The scrape loop does not recover panics, so Prometheus crashed.

Histograms are now validated before synthesis uses them. Invalid ones are returned unchanged, so they are rejected on append as they are without synthesis, and the anchor and the previous sample stay as they were. When the feature is enabled, this adds one `Validate` call per histogram sample.

Two existing tests used integer histograms whose count did not match their buckets, which validation rejects. I added the missing bucket counts. No assertions changed.

prs.title: discovery/linode: fix transfer allowance conversion
prs.body:
Linode reports transfer allowances in GiB, but discovery converts them using a MiB multiplier. This makes `__meta_linode_specs_transfer_bytes` 1,024 times too small.

Use the GiB-to-bytes conversion and update all seven existing table-driven expectations. For example, `transfer: 4000` now produces `4294967296000` bytes instead of `4194304000`.

This matches [Akamai’s documented transfer units](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/understanding-how-billing-works#gb-vs-gib-conversion-of-bytes).

Validation:
- Confirmed the corrected expectations fail before the conversion fix.
- Passed `go test -race ./discovery/linode -count=1`.
- Passed `make lint GOLANGCI_LINT_OPTS=--timeout=10m`.

```release-notes
[BUGFIX] Linode SD: Fix `__meta_linode_specs_transfer_bytes` reporting values 1,024 times too small
```

prs.title: promtool: Report TSDB disk usage by metric name
prs.body:
This PR enhances the `--extended` flag of `promtool tsdb analyze` to provide a detailed breakdown of disk usage by metric name.

## Motivation

In some environments, disk retention has triggered earlier than expected, resulting in the loss of more historical data than intended. Existing analyses from `promtool tsdb analyze` (such as series or label pair counts) are insufficient to diagnose high disk usage. Metric name cardinality can increase due to label churn without a corresponding rise in disk consumption, and series with constant or infrequent values are efficiently compacted. As a result, it is difficult to identify which metrics are responsible for high disk usage.

## Implementation

This change iterates over all chunk files in a TSDB block, calculates the disk usage for each chunk according to the [TSDB chunk format documentation](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/tsdb/docs/format/chunks.md), and aggregates usage by metric name. The 8-byte header of ea
